title: perf-bench-scratch-michelle-wu-2026-03-20
content:
Quick scratchpad notes for latency/throughput runs (iterative).

Goal:
- Narrow down best default batching + KV-cache policy for Llama-2 style models (70B-ish) on H100. Tradeoff target: p95 latency <= 250ms for single-stream inference, while maximizing tokens/sec for batch workloads.

Environment / config:
- Hardware: single H100 80GB (DGXA-style node), CUDA 12.3, cuBLAS/cuDNN latest stack used in infra image.
- Model: open-70B-v2 (decoder-only), 1x shard (single-GPU) quantized -> nf4 (experimental) and fp16 runs for baseline.
- Runtime: serving-runtime branch perf/kv-batching-2026 (local build) + our redis-backed prefix cache disabled/enabled per run.
- Sequence lengths tested: 64, 256, 1024. Context length during runs: 2048 (KV-cache capacity set accordingly).
- Batch sizes: [1, 4, 8, 16] (request-level batching). Continuous batching window: 5ms and 15ms explored.
- Prompt pattern: short system + user ~30 tokens, gen target 128 tokens.

Notes on measurement methodology:
- Each run: 200 warmup inferences, then 500 measured inferences. P50/p95/p99 latencies recorded per-token and end-to-end (request->final token). Throughput measured as tokens/sec observed by the runtime. GPU memory sampled with nvidia-smi every 2s.
- CPU and network traffic minimal (local), so ignore remote variance.
- Key metric flags: p95_end2end_ms, p50_token_ms, tokens_per_sec.

Results (summary table):

Run ID | Quant | Batch | Batching window | KV-cache | p50_e2e_ms | p95_e2e_ms | tokens/sec | GPU_mem_GB | Notes
R1     | fp16  | 1     | 5ms             | off      | 110        | 220       | 4200       | 62         | baseline
R2     | nf4   | 1     | 5ms             | off      | 95         | 190       | 4700       | 54         | nf4 wins on mem and throughput
R3     | nf4   | 4     | 5ms             | off      | 180        | 340       | 8800       | 58         | higher throughput, p95 > target
R4     | nf4   | 4     | 15ms            | off      | 160        | 300       | 9200       | 58         | longer window helps p95 slightly
R5     | nf4   | 4     | 5ms             | on       | 130        | 230       | 11000      | 58         | KV cache reduces compute, increases throughput
R6     | nf4   | 8     | 15ms            | on       | 220        | 420       | 16500      | 59         | good throughput but p95 too high for single-stream SLAs
R7     | fp16  | 1     | 5ms             | on       | 100        | 205       | 4800       | 62         | fp16 + cache ~= nf4 no-cache throughput
R8     | nf4   | 2     | 5ms             | on       | 120        | 210       | 7300       | 56         | sweet spot for mixed workloads

Observations:
- Quantization to nf4 gives ~10-15% throughput boost and reduces GPU memory by ~6-10GB vs fp16 in these configs.
- KV-cache ON provides the best improvements when there is prefix reuse (our prompt pattern had repeated system tokens and short user tokens). For gen=128 it improved tokens/sec by ~20-30% depending on batch.
- Small batching (batch=2 or 4) with KV-cache on + 5ms batching window hits a good latency/throughput tradeoff (R5, R8). p95 around 210-230ms which is close to our 250ms target.
- Large batch sizes (8 or 16) push tokens/sec up but p95 degrades (due to batching queuing) — not acceptable for low-latency product routes.
- Increasing batching window from 5ms->15ms sometimes reduces p95 slightly for medium batches (likely better coalescing), but adds tail latency for single-shot requests. So default should be 5ms with option to configure per-route.

Weirdness / anomalies:
- Observed occasional p99 spikes (~>700ms) in R6 only; correlates with host GPU clock scaling (power manager kicking in). Need to pin clocks for controlled runs.
- Memory sampling showed transient ~2-3GB bumps in nf4 runs when cache warmed — likely due to allocations for KV structures. Investigate allocator fragmentation.

Quick conclusions / recommendation (for defaults):
- Default quant: nf4 for hosted/dedicated where we want lower mem footprint; fallback to fp16 for customers that require max accuracy (can A/B).
- Default batching window: 5ms, default per-route max batch: 4. Default route config: batching=4, kv_cache=enabled for routes with >10% prefix reuse expected.
- Offer a latency-preserving mode: per-route batching cap=2 + kv_cache ON + early-flush after 3ms for ultra-low-latency endpoints.
- Add automated clock pin check in perf harness to avoid power-management variance.

Next steps / experiments to run:
- Repeat R5/R8 on H100 multi-GPU sharded config (2xH100) to confirm scaling behaviors.
- Test with longer generate (512 tokens) to see how KV-cache benefits grow and where memory pressure starts to dominate.
- Run same matrix with sequence length 1024 prompt to evaluate attention kernel performance change.
- Add perf runs with compilation knob XLA-like kernel selection enabled (branch perf/kernel-tuner).

Notes to self:
- Link perf plots to confluence page (linked_artifacts above) after final pass.
- Bring up p99 spike with infra team (ENG-SRE).
- Chat with Ethan and Sam about adding allocator debug prints.

-- Michelle

(End of scratchpad)
